No. d6s were used to determine a lot. Look at the referee book p. 103 (specialists and thieves). "But that's just for..."

Hold on.

Flip over to the Rules Book. P. 16 Elves "Elves’ enhanced senses allow them to detect secret doors more often than

others (2 in 6 chance)," so what about others? Now p. 53 "Hidden items or features have a base 1 in 6 chance of being found per turn of searching."

That's right. Any noob can look and gets a 1 in 6 chance, but elven noobs get a 2 in 6 chance.

Now, LotFP is based on Basic D&D, which also Labyrinth Lord is based off of. Here are ways I handle some checks in LL:

  • arcane knowledge check (magic-users and illusionists 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

  • geography check (magic-users, illusionists, clerics, druids and rangers 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

  • history knowledge check (monks, magic-users and illusionists 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

  • knowledge of the planes check (magic-users and clerics 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

  • military engineering check (fighters, paladins and rangers 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

  • nature check (druids and rangers 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

  • nobility knowledge check (fighters, clerics, magic-users, illusionists, paladins and rangers 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

  • religion check (clerics and paladins 1-2 in d6, others 1 in 6)

Another option is rolling under a stat. Oh, you need to leap across a wide gap, well, roll under your Dex to do that.

thanks a bunch, when it came to spells I know I will have them start with spells, but how do I go about awarding them with spells later on? or Is leaving remains of a magic book or scroll for them to find and copy over acceptable?

Magic Book, p. 11

>"If a Magic-User wishes to add a spell to a spellbook without a prior reference of the spell (a scroll or another spellbook), there is more intensive research to be done. A Magic-User may only research spells of a level he is able to cast."

Now the important bit is that the magic-user is researching a spell without a scroll (note: it's cheaper to research a magic-user spell already in the lists; that's one way). If Fnord the Magnificent finds a scroll of light, he can cast read magic, read the light spell and transcribe it to his spellbook (Magic Book p. 10). In LotFP all this costs money and time, in fact a lot in LotFP is about money and time.
